name: Celery Shipping – Comunas de Chile y Envíos Personalizados
author: Celery Software LLC

sections.description:
Celery Shipping adapts WooCommerce to the Chilean market and solves, through configuration fields and without writing any code, the most common shipping rule in the country: a base cost, an included weight, and a surcharge for every kilo above it.

For example: 3,990 CLP up to 5 kg, plus 500 CLP for each additional kilo, for a selected group of communes.

The plugin ships two independent modules that can be switched on or off separately, so you can use only the part you need.

Localization module

Adds the 346 communes of Chile to the checkout as a dropdown that depends on the selected region, but only when the address being edited is set to Chile. Customers from any other country keep their regular city text field exactly as WooCommerce ships it; this module never touches it.

It does not replace the sixteen Chilean regions that WooCommerce already ships: it uses them, with their existing ISO codes, so your saved addresses stay valid even if you deactivate the plugin.

The commune data is grouped by region following the political-administrative division published by the Library of the National Congress of Chile, and the commune names were cross-checked against the commune table of the Chilean Internal Revenue Service (SII).

Commune shipping module

Adds a shipping method you place inside any WooCommerce shipping zone. For each rate you set:

  • the base cost,
  • the weight that base cost already covers (“included weight”),
  • the price for every extra kilo above that weight, rounded up,
  • the exact communes the rate applies to,
  • an optional maximum weight above which the rate is not offered.

An included weight of 0 means the surcharge applies from the very first kilo. To make the base cost cover any weight regardless of the cart, leave the price per extra kilo at 0 instead.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. It requires WooCommerce to be active.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Celery Shipping CL and check that the modules you want are switched on. Both are on by default.
  3. If you are going to use the shipping module, go to WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping and open a shipping zone.
  4. Click Add shipping method and choose Celery — Commune shipping.
  5. Edit the method and fill in the fields: title, base cost, included weight, price per additional kilo, and the communes where it applies.
sections.faq:
Can I use only the regions and communes, with another shipping plugin?

Yes. Turn the Commune shipping module off in the settings tab and leave the Localization module on. The dependent checkout dropdown keeps working alongside any other shipping plugin.

Does it replace the Chilean regions that WooCommerce already has?

No, and that is deliberate. WooCommerce already ships the sixteen Chilean regions with their ISO codes, and this plugin uses them as they are. Only the commune is added, in the city field.

Does it affect checkout for customers outside Chile?

No. The city field only turns into a commune dropdown when that address is set to Chile. Addresses from every other country keep the normal free-text city field, unmodified.

How is the surcharge calculated?

The base cost is charged up to the included weight. Above that, the price per additional kilo is added for every extra kilo, rounded up. An order of 6 kg with 5 kg included is charged the base cost plus one extra kilo. If the included weight is set to 0, the surcharge applies from the first kilo.

Does it work with the block checkout?

The shipping method does, because the rate is calculated on the server. The dependent commune dropdown is built for the classic (shortcode) checkout; in the block checkout the commune stays a free text field, and the rate still finds it because commune matching ignores accents, letter case and punctuation.

A commune is missing or is spelled differently. What do I do?

Report it on the plugin support forum and mention the region. Note that several official Chilean sources spell a few communes differently, so the plugin also accepts the known variants.

What happens to my data if I uninstall the plugin?

Deactivating the plugin never deletes anything. Only deleting it from Plugins > Installed Plugins can, and by default it does not touch your shipping rates: it removes just this plugin’s own settings (including the two module toggles, which go back to being both enabled if you reinstall). If you want a full cleanup, go to WooCommerce > Settings > Celery Shipping CL before deleting the plugin and choose “Delete everything, including my shipping rates” under Uninstall. Either way, your orders and your customers’ addresses are never touched.
